hero.title: Phidao
hero.subtitle: The members' council for the Phiegg economy.
hero.body: Phidao is where members propose, debate and vote on the rules of the shared economy — token functions, treasury spend, fees and launch policy. Votes are weighted by Phiput (PFT) holdings. Any member can propose; the treasury executes what passes.

params.passThreshold: Simple majority of votes cast, quorum met

proposals.title: Lower quest listing fees by half
proposals.summary: Cut quest listing fees from 40 to 20 $EGG for clubs under a year old.
proposals.body: New clubs carry the heaviest listing costs just as they are finding holders. This halves the quest listing fee for any club less than twelve months old, funded by a 0.1% increase in the Phidao swap fee. Reviewed by the Phisum working group; treasury impact is net neutral by month three.

proposals.title: Fund a runway week in Runway Hall
proposals.summary: Treasury funds one week of shows in Runway Hall, open to all launched clubs.
proposals.body: Allocate 180,000 USDC for a shared runway week: staging, agent choreography and capture, with slots balloted across launched clubs. Expected to lift secondary floor across participating clubs based on the Spring show.

proposals.title: Add a 'fitting' PFT function
proposals.summary: Introduce a standard 'fitting' function so looks can be tried on across worlds.
proposals.body: Define 'fitting' as a first-class PFT function with a shared interface, so a look bought in one world can be previewed in another. Requires a Phisum schema change and a reference implementation from Phinux.

proposals.title: Cap host creation at 5 per member per month
proposals.summary: Rate-limit new hosts to curb spam after the summer surge.
proposals.body: Introduces a soft cap of five new hosts per member per month, liftable by holding 50+ Phiput. Passed with 68% in favour.

proposals.title: Route 0.3% swap fee to the treasury
proposals.summary: Formalise the Phidao swap fee and its destination.
proposals.body: Codifies the existing 0.3% swap fee and directs it entirely to the Phidao treasury, replacing the previous split with Phisum.

proposals.title: Grant Phinux a maintenance budget
proposals.summary: Standing quarterly budget for the Phinux toolchain.
proposals.body: Allocate 60,000 USDC per quarter to Phinux for engine and SDK maintenance, reviewed each quarter.

proposals.title: Require verified contracts for direct launch
proposals.summary: Mandate contract verification before a club can skip Phipad.
proposals.body: Would have required every directly-launched club to verify its contract on-chain first. Rejected 54% to 46%; seen as too heavy for small clubs.

proposals.title: Seasonal grants for agentic worlds
proposals.summary: A seasonal grant pool for agent-populated worlds.
proposals.body: Create a 250,000 USDC seasonal pool for agentic-world experiments, administered with Phipad's agentic track.

news.body: The 0.3% Phidao swap fee is now codified and directed entirely to the treasury.

about.body: Phidao governs the rules the rest of Phiace runs on. It does not hold your items or your wallet — it decides the shared parameters: which PFT functions exist, how the treasury spends, what fees apply, and the policy around launching clubs.

sections.title: How a proposal works
sections.body: Any member can draft a proposal and stake 100 $SUM to open it. It runs for five days. Votes are weighted by your Phiput (PFT) holdings. If turnout meets the 1,800 PFT quorum and a simple majority is in favour, the treasury executes it; otherwise the stake is returned and the proposal closes.

sections.title: Voting weight
sections.body: One Phiput is one vote. You can vote yourself or delegate your weight to someone who votes the way you would — delegation is revocable at any time and shows on the Delegates page.

sections.title: The treasury
sections.body: Funded by swap fees, primary-mint royalties and protocol revenue. Every inflow and outflow is on the Treasury page. Spends above 100,000 USDC always require a proposal.

sections.title: Relationship to Phisum
sections.body: Phidao sets policy; Phisum holds the PFT function registry and executes schema changes a proposal approves. The two are deliberately separate so governance and mechanism can be audited apart.

faq.a: Any member holding Phiput (PFT). Your weight equals your holdings at the time the proposal opened.

faq.q: What does it cost to propose?
faq.a: A 100 $SUM stake, returned when the proposal closes unless it is withdrawn early.

faq.q: What happens if quorum is not met?
faq.a: The proposal fails regardless of the yes/no split, and the stake is returned.
Yes, any time before voting closes. Delegated weight can also be reclaimed at any time.
